definitions.explanation: a device for making holes in paper, typically for inserting into binders

examples.japanese: {穴|あな}あけパンチで{書類|しょるい}に{穴|あな}をあける。
examples.english: To punch holes in documents with a hole punch.

examples.japanese: この{穴|あな}あけパンチは{二|に}{穴|あな}{用|よう}だ。
examples.english: This hole punch is for making two holes.

examples.japanese: {穴|あな}あけパンチの{位置|いち}を{調整|ちょうせい}する。
examples.english: To adjust the position of the hole punch.

notes:
A device used to punch holes in paper so it can be inserted into a ring binder or file. Standard in Japanese offices and schools.

ALSO CALLED:
- パンチ (punch) — abbreviated form, most common in speech
- {穴|あな}あけ{器|き} (hole maker) — less common variant

TYPES:
- {二|に}{穴|あな}パンチ (2-hole punch) — standard in Japan
- {一|いち}{穴|あな}パンチ (single hole punch)
- {多|た}{穴|あな}パンチ (multi-hole punch)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {穴|あな}あけパンチで{穴|あな}をあける: to punch holes
- パンチで{書類|しょるい}をとじる{準備|じゅんび}をする: to prepare documents for filing

RELATED TERMS:
- バインダー (binder)
- ファイル (file/folder)
- ホチキス (stapler)
